issues.failure_explanation: The numerator satisfies $\phi^2|\psi|^2-|\phi|^2\psi^2=(\phi\overline{\psi}-\overline{\phi}\psi)(\phi\overline{\psi}+\overline{\phi}\psi)$, but the displayed reduction keeps only the first factor and also divides by $|\phi||\psi|$, which is undefined at zeros. The subsequent pointwise bound is therefore not justified by the displayed chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unit-fraction manipulation by a max-based estimate, namely $|U_\phi-U_\psi|\le 2|\phi-\psi|/\max(|\phi|,|\psi|)$ with $U_\phi=\phi^2/|\phi|^2$ defined by continuity at zeros, together with $|f'(\rho_\psi)|\psi|^2|\le C|\psi|^{1+\theta}$; this yields the stated pointwise bound directly.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the Hessian Lipschitz estimate in Proposition Property-of-E''-(iii), and consequently the later uses of that estimate in Property-P, Polyak-Loj, C_t, and the convergence theorems, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Invalid algebra in the Hessian continuity estimate
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained pointwise estimate and preserves the proposition, its constant $p_0$, and all downstream uses, so the invalid algebra does not force any loss of result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $\tau_n\in (0,\tau_{\max})$, the iterations $\{\phi^n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ generated by the P-RG have the following properties:

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem permits $\tau_n\to0$. Then $C_{\tau_n}\ge \tau_n-\tau_n^2/\tau_{\max}}$ can also tend to $0$, so summability of the energy decreases does not imply $\|d_n\|\to0$. The proof nevertheless infers $\|\nabla^{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathcal{P}}E^n\|\to0$, which is the step used to obtain a critical subsequential limit.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a uniform positive lower bound on the step size, e.g. $\tau_n\ge\tau_0>0$, or equivalently assume $\inf_n C_{\tau_n}>0$; then infinitely many steps with gradient bounded away from zero would force a fixed energy drop, contradicting energy convergence.
issues.overall_effect: Part (ii) of Global-Convergence, namely subsequential convergence to a critical point, is unsupported for step sizes tending to zero; part (i) energy convergence remains valid.
issues.title: Global convergence proof allows vanishing step sizes
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single standard step-size restriction and preserves the practical constant-step global convergence result, but it excludes the advertised regime of arbitrary $\tau_n\in(0,\tau_{\max})$, so the scope of part (ii) is materially narrowed.

issues.failure_explanation: The retraction estimate gives $\|\phi^{j+1}-\phi^j\|=O(\|d_j\|)$, not $O(\|d_j\|^2)$. Since $\|d_j\|$ is small, there is no uniform inequality $\|d_j\|\le C\|d_j\|^2$, so the induction that keeps the iterates inside the neighborhood where PL and C_t apply is unjustified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the increments by $C\|d_j\|$ and then use the geometric estimate $\|d_j\|\le C(\sqrt{1-2C_\tau(\mu-\varepsilon)})^{j/2}$ already obtained in the same proof, so the sum remains uniformly bounded and the choice of $\sigma,\sigma_3$ is unchanged in substance.
issues.overall_effect: The invariant step in the proof of Local-Convergence fails, leaving the linear convergence rate and the later uses of that theorem in Var-P-convergence and Corollary E-eq-Phi without a valid foundation as written.
issues.title: Local convergence induction uses the wrong power of the descent direction
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local repair of one inequality using the geometric decay already proved; the theorem's neighborhood, rate, and step-size range survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the optimal local preconditioner does not satisfy {\bf (A6)}-$(iii)$, its global convergence cannot be guaranteed in general.
This weaker condition still ensures the validity of {\bf Proposition \ref{Property-P}}, thereby guaranteeing the local convergence of the algorithm.

issues.failure_explanation: Local-Convergence is proved under (A1)-(A6), while the text explicitly says that the optimal local preconditioner does not satisfy (A6)-(iii). The paper mentions a weaker local Lipschitz condition and asserts that the optimal preconditioner is Lipschitz, but it does not prove that this preconditioner satisfies the weaker condition in the norms required by the local theory before invoking Local-Convergence.

failure_location.quote: According to {\bf Theorem \ref{Local-Convergence}}, we already know that this sequence $\left\{\phi^n\right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is linearly convergent for all $\tau\in(0,2/(L+\varepsilon))$ and for any $\phi^0\in\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{S})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove, near $\phi_g$, that the optimal local preconditioner satisfies the weakened (A6)-(iii) together with the locally needed coercivity, continuity, and (A6)-(iv), and then invoke that weakened local convergence result explicitly; alternatively add this local regularity as a hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The first step of the proof of Var-P-convergence applies a theorem outside its stated assumptions, so the claimed optimal rate for the preconditioner $E''(\phi)-(\widetilde{\lambda}_\phi-\sigma_0)\\mathcal{I}$ is not established as written.
issues.title: Optimal-preconditioner theorem invokes local convergence outside its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The affected theorem is central, but the missing dependency can be repaired by a contained local verification of the weakened preconditioner assumptions; no new global proof architecture or change of rate is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The upper bound $L$ from Property-P-(i) is valid only for vectors in $N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$. But $\text{Proj}^{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}_{\phi_g}d_n$ is the $\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}$-orthogonal projection onto the full tangent space $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$, not the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto the normal space $N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$. Hence the subsequent bound by $L\|d_n\|^2_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}$ does not follow from the cited spectral estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the tangent projection by the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto $N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$, or equivalently subtract the components along $i\phi_g$ and $i\mathcal{L}_z\phi_g$; since $E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I}$ vanishes on $T\mathcal{S}$, the same upper bound follows.
issues.overall_effect: The local energy-dissipation lemma C_t has an invalid proof step, which propagates to the local convergence theorem, the optimal-preconditioner theorem, and the energy-wavefunction equivalence corollary.
issues.title: Local dissipation proof projects onto the tangent space instead of the normal space
issues.why_classification: The same dissipation estimate is recovered by a one-step change of projection using the already established vanishing of the Hessian on the symmetry directions; no rate or theorem statement is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, in this context, we have $\mu = (\lambda_3 - \lambda_g)\\big/(\lambda_3 - \lambda_g + \sigma_0)$ and $L = 1$.
Notably, a superlinear convergence rate (see \cite{2006Numerical}) is attainable when $\mu = L$.
which is the best rate one can possibly get for a Riemannian gradient method.

issues.failure_explanation: For the optimal local preconditioner and fixed $\sigma_0>0$, one has $\mu=(\lambda_3-\lambda_g)/(\lambda_3-\lambda_g+\sigma_0)<1=L$, so the proved rate $(L-\mu)/(L+\mu)+\varepsilon$ is still linear. It only tends to zero as $\sigma_0\downarrow0$; taking $\sigma_0=0$ would destroy coercivity on the symmetry directions and is outside the stated assumptions. The claim that $\mu=L$ gives superlinear convergence also conflicts with the theorem's quantifier, which keeps $\varepsilon>0$ and therefore gives a linear rate. The abstract's unqualified 'best possible' phrasing is likewise stronger than the paper's own later PL-only qualification.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, reducing $\sigma_0$ appropriately, one can achieve a P-RG with superlinear local  convergence rate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the overclaims by the theorem's content: for every fixed $\sigma_0>0$ the rate is linear with $\rho=(L-\mu)/(L+\mu)+\varepsilon$, and $\rho\downarrow0$ only in the limit $\sigma_0\downarrow0$; state explicitly that superlinear convergence is not proved under the given assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion and abstract promise a superlinear or unconditionally optimal rate that the formal theorems do not establish; the actual guaranteed result is a sharp linear rate for each fixed $\sigma_0>0$.
issues.title: Superlinear and unqualified optimal-rate claims overstate the theorems
issues.why_classification: The correction is prose-level and leaves the main linear optimal-rate theorem intact, but it necessarily withdraws an advertised superlinear guarantee and an unqualified optimality claim.
